adversarial_audit.notes: Reviewed all givens and solution. Equal run-on rules out transcriptional defect. Reciprocal 25-nt swap localizes cause to cis sequence. Insensitivity to increasing spliceosome factor rules out limiting trans factor. Retained RNAs are nuclear and UPF1 inhibition has no effect, ruling out cytoplasmic NMD. Intronless rescue adds +40 cytoplasmic mature-equivalent units: 20+40=60 vs G2=80 → 60:80 = 3:4. Choice A uniquely matches all evidence.

shortest_solution: Run-on equal → transcription rates equal, so steady-state RNA difference is post-transcriptional (rules out B).

25-nt boundary swap transfers intron-3 retention and retained RNAs are nuclear; intronless rescue increases cytoplasmic G1 without UPF1 effect → a cis-acting 25-nt element causes intron retention and nuclear sequestration, not NMD (rules out D).
Doubling a general spliceosome factor does nothing → not a limiting trans-acting splice factor (rules out C).
non_obvious_decisions: Select cis-acting 25-nt boundary as causal mechanism for intron retention and nuclear sequestration
Reject NMD (UPF1-mediated cytoplasmic decay) as mechanism based on lack of UPF1 effect and nuclear retention
Reject limiting trans-acting spliceosome factor mechanism based on no change when doubling the factor
difficulty_audit.notes: All observations point to a cis-acting 25-nt element causing nuclear intron retention and sequestration; rescue via intronless construct bypasses retention. The allele-specific minigene result in one shared nuclear extract is the hidden constraint that separates a cis sequence defect from global trans-acting alternatives.
